quests.instruction: Why should you not squeeze fruit hard at the shop?
quests.hint: Think about the next shopper.
quests.explanation: Squeezing hard leaves bruises, and bruised fruit spoils faster. A gentle touch is enough.
quests.funFact: Shops often display fruit in single layers so it does not get squashed.

quests.instruction: What is one advantage of buying loose fruit instead of a pre-packed bag?
quests.correctAnswer: You can choose exactly how many and pick each piece
options: It is always cheaper than the packaged kind of fruit
You can choose exactly how many and pick each piece
It never goes bad, even if you keep it a week
quests.hint: Think about choosing.
quests.explanation: Loose fruit lets you choose the number you need and check each piece for bruises.
quests.funFact: Pre-packed fruit is handy when you want a standard amount.

quests.instruction: Why does pre-cut fruit often cost more than a whole fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: Someone did the cutting and packaging work
options: It has more seeds and more flavor
Someone did the cutting and packaging work
It comes from special expensive trees
quests.hint: Think about the extra work.
quests.explanation: Pre-cut fruit costs more because someone peeled, cut and packaged it for you.
quests.funFact: Pre-cut fruit is convenient, but it should be kept cold.

quests.instruction: You need bananas for breakfast tomorrow and also for the weekend. What is a smart way to choose?
quests.correctAnswer: Buy some ripe ones and some greener ones
options: Buy only the very ripest ones you can find
Buy only hard green ones for both days
Buy some ripe ones and some greener ones
quests.hint: Think about how bananas change over a few days.
quests.explanation: Ripe bananas are ready now, while greener ones will ripen in a few days.
quests.funFact: Bananas at room temperature ripen steadily over several days.

quests.instruction: Which choice creates less waste when you buy fruit?
options: Use a new plastic bag for each fruit
quests.hint: Think about using something again and again.
quests.explanation: A reusable bag can be used many times, so it creates less waste.
quests.funFact: Sturdy reusable bags can be used hundreds of times.

quests.instruction: Grapes cost 6 coins per kilogram. How much do 500 grams cost?
quests.hint: 500 grams is half a kilogram.
quests.explanation: 500 grams is half a kilogram, and half of 6 coins is 3 coins.
quests.funFact: Shop scales often show the weight and price together.

quests.instruction: A team needs a quick fruit snack at halftime that is easy to share. Which fits?
quests.hint: Think about juicy and easy.
quests.explanation: Orange wedges are juicy, easy to share and ready to eat without tools.
quests.funFact: Orange wedges are a classic snack at many kids' sports games.

quests.instruction: Which lunchbox includes fruit along with other kinds of food?
options: A bag of candy and a soft drink
A packet of crackers and a cookie
quests.hint: Think about several food groups in one lunchbox.
quests.explanation: A lunchbox with fruit and other foods gives a nice variety.
quests.funFact: Lunchboxes with different colors of food are often more fun to eat.

quests.instruction: Which fruit platter is best for a party?
quests.correctAnswer: A colorful mix cut into bite-size pieces
options: One huge uncut watermelon for everyone
Only whole fruits with large hard pits
A colorful mix cut into bite-size pieces
quests.hint: Think about what is easy for guests to pick up.
quests.explanation: A colorful mix of bite-size pieces is easy to eat and looks inviting.
quests.funFact: A platter looks best when the colors alternate.

quests.instruction: Which fruit adds a sweet, juicy pop of color to a green salad?
quests.hint: Think of tiny red jewels.
quests.explanation: Pomegranate seeds add color, sweetness and a juicy pop to salads.
quests.funFact: Pomegranate seeds are often sprinkled on salads and rice dishes in the Middle East.

quests.instruction: Which fruit gives us a creamy milk used in many curries and desserts?
quests.hint: Think about pressing the white flesh with water.
quests.explanation: Coconut milk is made by pressing grated coconut flesh with water, and it is used in many curries and desserts.
quests.funFact: Coconut milk comes from the flesh, not from the water inside the coconut.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is often served with cheese on a snack board?
quests.hint: Think of a fruit that is bite-sized.
quests.explanation: Grapes are bite-sized and pair well with cheese on a snack board.
quests.funFact: Pears and apples are also served with cheese in many countries.

quests.instruction: A shopper describes it: dusty purple skin, eaten with the skin on, one hard pit, and its dried form has a special name. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Think about prunes.
quests.explanation: Plum fits every clue. Cherries have long stems and are smaller, and grapes have no hard pit.
quests.funFact: Plum trees often bloom in early spring, sometimes before their leaves appear.

quests.instruction: Soft teardrop shape, tiny seeds, thin skin you can eat, sold fresh or dried and chewy. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Think of a fruit with a gentle crunch inside.
quests.explanation: Fig fits every clue. Mango has a large stone and kiwi has fuzzy skin.
quests.funFact: Figs are eaten fresh in summer and dried the rest of the year in many places.

quests.instruction: Green skin, pink flesh, many hard seeds, eaten with the skin on. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Think of a fruit with a strong sweet smell.
quests.explanation: Guava fits every clue. Pear has a core and papaya has black seeds in a hollow center.
quests.funFact: A ripe guava smells strongly sweet even from a distance.

quests.instruction: Small, flat, orange, with loose skin that peels easily and juicy segments. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Think of a favorite lunchbox citrus.
quests.explanation: Mandarin fits every clue. Lemon is yellow and sour, and pomelo is huge with a thick peel.
quests.funFact: In many countries, mandarins are a favorite lunchbox fruit because the peel comes off easily.

quests.instruction: Bell-shaped, a little gritty when ripe, usually bought firm and ripened at home. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Think of the neck near the stem.
quests.explanation: Pear fits every clue. Apples are rounder and crunchier, and peaches have a pit.
quests.funFact: Pears have a core with small seeds instead of a pit.

quests.instruction: Round with netted skin, orange flesh, a hollow middle full of seeds and a smooth scar where the stem was. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Think of a sweet melon.
quests.explanation: Cantaloupe fits every clue. Pomelo and pineapple do not have hollow, seed-filled centers.
quests.funFact: A cantaloupe's net pattern grows as the fruit gets bigger.

quests.instruction: A friend brings a fruit you have never seen. What is a friendly thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask what it is and try a small bite
options: Say that it looks strange and refuse it
Ask what it is and try a small bite
Hide it in your bag without trying
quests.hint: Think about being curious and kind.
quests.explanation: Being curious and polite makes trying new foods friendly.
quests.funFact: Every country has fruits that are favorites at home but unknown elsewhere.

quests.instruction: A recipe needs both the zest and the juice of one lemon. Which order is easier?
quests.hint: Which is easier to grate: a whole lemon or a squeezed half?
quests.explanation: A whole lemon is easier to grate than a squeezed half, so zest first and then juice.
quests.funFact: Lemon zest holds the fragrant oils, which is why a little adds so much flavor.

quests.instruction: A sticker on a fruit says "organic." What does that mean?
quests.correctAnswer: It was grown following organic farming rules
options: It is always sweeter than other kinds of fruit
It was grown indoors in water without any soil
It was grown following organic farming rules
quests.hint: Think about how the fruit was grown.
quests.explanation: Organic means the fruit was grown following certain farming rules. It still needs washing.
quests.funFact: Organic and non-organic fruit both need washing.

quests.instruction: You used half a lime. How should you store the other half?
options: Open on the counter for a week
quests.hint: Think about keeping it from drying out.
quests.explanation: A cut lime dries out quickly, so keep it covered in the fridge.
quests.funFact: Cut citrus dries out quickly when left uncovered.

quests.instruction: A whole watermelon is too big for your family. What can you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Buy a half or a quarter of one
options: Buy three whole ones to be safe
Buy a half or a quarter of one
Skip watermelon and buy only juice
quests.hint: Think about buying only what you need.
quests.explanation: Many shops sell cut halves or quarters so you can buy just what you need.
quests.funFact: Smaller, personal-sized watermelons are grown too.

quests.instruction: Your lemon feels hard and gives little juice. What can help?
quests.correctAnswer: Roll it firmly on the counter before cutting
options: Roll it firmly on the counter before cutting
Freeze it for a full day before cutting
Dip it in sugar water for ten minutes first
quests.hint: Think about loosening the juicy segments.
quests.explanation: Rolling a lemon firmly on the counter helps break up the juicy segments, so more juice comes out.
quests.funFact: Room-temperature lemons often give more juice than cold ones.

quests.instruction: You have 12 coins. Apples cost 3 coins each and a bunch of grapes costs 5 coins. Which way spends 11 coins?
quests.hint: Add up each choice.
quests.explanation: 2 apples cost 6 coins and the grapes cost 5, which makes 11 coins.
quests.funFact: Planning a shopping list helps you stay within a budget.

quests.instruction: A shop sells some fruit by the piece and some by weight. Which is most likely sold by the piece?
quests.correctAnswer: One whole pineapple with its crown
options: Loose cherries scooped from a bin
A heap of loose grapes in a bag
One whole pineapple with its crown
quests.hint: Think about fruit you would count one by one.
quests.explanation: Large single fruits like pineapples are often counted and priced by the piece, while small fruits like cherries and grapes are usually sold by weight.
quests.funFact: Some shops sell melons by weight and others by the piece.

quests.instruction: How many 500 gram bags of grapes make 1 kilogram?
quests.hint: 1 kilogram is 1,000 grams.
quests.explanation: 1 kilogram is 1,000 grams, and 500 plus 500 makes 1,000.
quests.funFact: The word kilo means thousand, so a kilogram is a thousand grams.

quests.instruction: A fruit tastes very sour. How can you make a snack nicer without adding sugar?
quests.correctAnswer: Mix it with a sweeter fruit
options: Cook it with a lot of salt
Mix it with a sweeter fruit
Leave it out for a few weeks
quests.hint: Think about balancing flavors.
quests.explanation: Pairing a sour fruit like kiwi or grapefruit with sweeter fruit balances the flavors naturally.
quests.funFact: Cooks often balance sweet, sour, salty and bitter tastes.

quests.instruction: Which kitchen job is a good one for a child helping with fruit?
options: Slicing a pineapple with a big knife
Carrying a pot of boiling water
quests.hint: Think about a safe, helpful job.
quests.explanation: Washing fruit is a safe, helpful job. Big knives and hot pots are for grown-ups.
quests.funFact: Even small helpers can arrange fruit on a plate.

quests.instruction: You want to try growing fruit at home in a small space. Which is the best choice to start with?
quests.hint: Think about a plant that stays small.
quests.explanation: Strawberry plants stay small and grow well in pots, while coconut palms and jackfruit trees grow very large.
quests.funFact: Pots with drainage holes help roots stay healthy.
